  "text": "At the alterations shop, Helen laid her coat across the counter.

“The lining’s gone,” she said.

The woman turned back the sleeve. A strip of blue fabric hung loose at the cuff.

“Both sides?”

“Just that one, I think.”

The woman checked the other sleeve anyway. Behind her, trousers hung from a rail with paper tickets pinned to their waistbands.

“I can patch it. A new lining would cost more than the coat.”

Helen nodded. Her mother had bought it for her first winter at the council offices. They had disagreed about the colour, then eaten sandwiches in the car because the café was full.

“Friday all right?”

“Yes.”

“Empty the pockets first.”

Helen took out her gloves, a receipt, and three wrapped mints. In the inside pocket, her fingers found something stiff and narrow.

It was a photograph from a machine: four pictures of her mother trying to sit at the correct height. In the first, only her forehead showed. In the last, she was laughing at someone outside the frame.

Helen remembered holding the shopping bags. She had been impatient to get home.

“Anything else?” the woman asked.

“No. That’s everything.”

Outside, rain was collecting along the bus shelter’s metal seat. Helen stood beneath the roof and put the mints into her handbag.

She kept the photograph in her hand until the bus came. Then she slipped it between two cards in her purse, leaving her mother’s face visible above them.

When she sat down, she reached to unbutton the coat she had left behind."
